content:
RBI Maintains Stance on Inflation & Liquidity

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) concluded its bimonthly meeting, deciding to hold the benchmark repo rate at 6.50%. This marks consecutive policy reviews where borrowing rates have been maintained steady to manage retail inflation while supporting economic expansion across India.

📌 Key Takeaway for Borrowers: Because the benchmark rate remains unchanged, banks will not increase their External Benchmark Linked Rates (EBLR). Your existing floating loan tenure and monthly EMI amount will stay stable.

title: New CIBIL Score Rules: How Multiple Hard Inquiries Now Impact Your Loan Sanction
tldr: Credit bureaus now refresh borrower repayment and inquiry data every 15 days instead of monthly.
Submitting loan applications across 4+ banks simultaneously can deduct 25 to 50 points from your CIBIL.
Soft inquiries made through certified financial DSA advisors like BFS do not hurt your credit profile.
A credit score above 720 remains the benchmark for instant unsecured loan approvals.
content:
Fortnightly Credit Reporting Now Active Across India

Under revised RBI directions for credit reporting transparency, all Scheduled Commercial Banks and NBFCs are now required to furnish consumer credit data to bureaus (TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF High Mark) every 15 days. Previously, data updates were compiled only once per month, allowing lags in reporting.

⚠️ Beware of Multiple Direct Bank Inquiries: When you apply directly to multiple portals at once, each lender registers a 'Hard Credit Pull'. Too many hard pulls within 30 days flags the borrower as 'credit-hungry', triggering automated algorithmic loan rejection.

How to Safeguard Your Credit Score

Borrowers looking for financing should follow three cardinal rules:

  1. Check Single Institutional Windows: Use BFS Financial Services to assess eligibility across 40+ lending institutions using a single soft-pull profile.
  2. Maintain Credit Utilization Below 30%: Avoid maxing out your credit cards even if you pay the full amount before the due date.
  3. Verify Account Status: Ensure old settled loans have received a formal 'No Objection Certificate' (NOC) and reflect as 'Closed' on your bureau report.
